unresolved.area: enemy kinds / audio - death sounds are cut by the new owner mechanism
unresolved.problem: New problem introduced by the revision (the owner / stopOwner mechanism). The contract tells every kind to play ALL its sounds with owner: actor.id, including the death sound in onKilled, and at the same time tells the manager to call ctx.audio.stopOwner(id) again when the slot is freed. Three engineers write seven kinds from this text; the result is silent deaths that no automated check catches. unresolved.area: boss death cleanup / player / director - the player can die during the staged death and no rule says who wins
unresolved.problem: New problem introduced by the fix for the 'after the run ends' finding. On a boss death the manager now kills every other live enemy as a NON-silent world kill, so onKilled runs for each of them. A tick's onKilled is where its blast lives (the contract routes proximity detonation through kill() too), so the up to 5 ticks summoned in phase 3, which by design are next to the player, all explode within 0.6 s of the boss dying (45 dmg, r = 5 m each; x1.6 on Nightmare). The mode stays 'playing' for the whole staged death (deathSeconds = 5), and takeDamage is only absorbed outside 'playing', so the player can die right after killing the boss. The contract then has two END OF RUN rules with no precedence: 'player:died' -> endRun(false) after 1.5 s, and 'boss:defeated' -> endRun(true) after sequenceSeconds. Read literally the run ends in game over 1.5 s after the boss was defeated. The same gap exists in the other order (boss killed by a rocket in flight after the player died). The director stub silently invents 'first event wins' and sets phase 'done' on death; neither is in the contract. A tick kind cannot tell 'I detonated myself' from 'the manager / director / bounds cull removed me': both arrive as weapon 'world'. The stub also skips onKilled for an actor that is still arriving, which the contract does not say.

assessment:
All 37 findings of the gameplay review (2 blockers, 21 major, 14 minor) are closed in the revised tree: none is left unresolved or only partly applied. I read /home/user/Testing-2/src/core/types.ts in full, plus core (game.ts, time.ts, bot.ts, debug.ts, constants.ts, make.ts, the input.ts bindings and lock handling), all of src/data, every stub and tools/. Nothing was edited and no build or test was run, so type-correctness of the tree is not confirmed by me.

Both blockers are really closed:
- Staged death: EnemyHandle.dying, onKilled returning corpse seconds, updateDying(dt, playerDt), the corpse timer on ctx.time.playerDt, and 'boss:defeated'.sequenceSeconds taken from onKilled.
- Boss phase: mutable phase / phaseCount / invulnerable / name on EnemyActor, EnemySystem.setBossPhase as the only emitter of 'boss:phase', and the manager absorbing hits while invulnerable.

Three proposed sub-items were deliberately not applied and are harmless to leave: EnemySpawnOptions.noDrops, ProjectileOptions.shotId, and the ring / sweep hit-test formulas (these stay inside the conductor kind, which drives the visual itself through setRadius).

Consistency checks that came out clean:
- Every FxId, SoundId and LoopId sits in exactly one owner union; FX_STREAM_IDS matches the 13 ids marked STREAM.
- Every event the contract assigns to core is emitted in core.
- No removed id ('boltFire', 'uiPerkSelect', 'shard', 'cinematic', 'pickupHum' and the rest) is still referenced in src or tools.
- Core, data, stubs and tools agree with the contract on the new clocks, the always-queued explosions, the per-target hit flush, kill credit, the two integrators, attack tokens and the debug API.

What remains are four NEW problems created by the revision's own fixes, each fixable with doc wording (no signature change):
1. Major: death sounds played with owner: actor.id, as the SoundId doc instructs, are cut 60 ms later by the manager's stopOwner at despawn.
2. Major: the boss-death cleanup kills ticks non-silently next to a still-vulnerable player, and the contract has no precedence between 'player:died' and 'boss:defeated'. Only the director stub decides it.
3. Minor: kill({ creditPlayer: true }) contradicts the rule that weapon 'world' kills are never rewarded.
4. Minor: a boss removed silently by error containment leaves the director in phase 'boss' for ever.

I would fix items 1 and 2 before the freeze, because three enemy engineers plus the player and director engineers would otherwise each guess.
